# Incident Report: Malware Infection — Host DESKTOP-H8ALZBV

**Case reference:** mta-2024-08-15
**Evidence analyzed:** `2024-08-15-traffic-analysis-exercise.pcap` (18,189 packets, 2024-08-15 04:09:43 – 04:42:26 UTC, ~32 min)
**Tooling:** tshark, capinfos, file, shasum (no internet lookups used)

## 1. Infected host

| Attribute | Value | Evidence |
|---|---|---|
| IPv4 address | **10.8.15.133** | Source of all malicious traffic |
| MAC address | **00:1c:bf:03:54:82** | DHCP request frames |
| Windows hostname | **DESKTOP-H8ALZBV** | DHCP Option 12 hostname; NBNS name registration (`<00>`, `<20>`) |
| AD domain | `lafontainebleu.org` (DC: `WIN-JEGJIX7Q9RS.lafontainebleu.org`, 10.8.15.4) | DNS SRV lookups for `_kerberos._tcp`, `_ldap._tcp` |
| Logged-in Windows user | **plucero** | Kerberos AS-REQ/TGS-REQ `CNameString` fields showing principal `plucero` alongside the machine account `DESKTOP-H8ALZBV$` |

## 2. Malware family

**GootLoader-style obfuscated JScript downloader**, leading to a persistent HTTP-based bot/RAT C2 channel.

**Attribution basis: behavioral, not signature-confirmed.** No AV/YARA match, JA3 database, or threat-intel lookup was performed (per scope — no internet use). The identification rests on the distinctive obfuscation technique observed directly in the recovered script:
- The downloaded `.js` is padded to **6,990,020 bytes** with megabytes of benign scraped document text (MPI programming manual, IPCC climate reports, PIAAC literacy survey text) — a well-known technique for inflating file size to evade AV/sandbox size and entropy heuristics.
- The actual malicious logic is interleaved inside `/* ... */` comment blocks as short JScript fragments with randomized camelCase identifiers, e.g.:
  `try{function gCTUXsDIEY884(teIBKLTf1, AYZmAnK2, ofwsZjP3, xSMzVYuDq4, UqjIss5) {`
  `SdmJEt += 'W5cwKH';`
- `WScript.Sleep` is present (evasion/delay before beaconing), consistent with a Windows Script Host (WSH) execution chain (`Invoice-*.js` → `wscript.exe`).
- Execution timeline confirms this: the invoice ZIP/JS is fetched at **t+74.7s**; the first outbound C2 connection begins at **t+134.8s** — a ~60-second gap matching a sleep-based sandbox-evasion delay before the downloader phones home.

This combination (fake shipping-invoice lure → oversized garbage-padded `.js` in a ZIP → delayed C2 beacon) is consistent with GootLoader/GootLoader-style loader tradecraft. No second-stage payload content was recoverable from the pcap (C2 traffic is encrypted), so I cannot confirm the final-stage RAT/backdoor family with certainty.

## 3. Indicators of compromise (all observed directly in traffic)

**Malicious domains**
- `quote.checkfedexexp.com` — fake FedEx phishing/lure domain, resolves to 104.21.55.70 / 172.67.170.159
- `business.checkfedexexp.com` — same phishing domain infrastructure, same IPs

**Malicious URL (initial delivery)**
- `http://quote.checkfedexexp.com/managements?16553a25e45250a41fd5&endeds=MIGpq&JStx=59bf050d37df88a9-ade43358-eaa1220b-0571422b-0f33e6aa150e86bafd0ed4&Ld=9d7502d88d752a27b1d00587309184b5a215`
  (UA: `Mozilla/5.0 (Windows NT 10.0; Win64; x64) ... Chrome/127.0.0.0 ... Edg/127.0.0.0` — real Edge browser fetching the lure)

**Transferred file / hashes**
- Delivered as ZIP, unpacked to: **`Invoice-876597035-003-8331775-8334138.js`**
  - SHA256 (extracted `.js`): `dab98819d1d7677a60f5d06be210d45b74ae5fd8cf0c24ec1b3766e25ce6dc2c`
  - SHA256 (ZIP container as transferred over HTTP): `798563fcf7600f7ef1a35996291a9dfb5f9902733404dd499e2e736ea1dc6fc5`

**Command-and-control endpoint**
- **72.5.43.29:80** — raw IP, no DNS lookup preceded it (hardcoded C2 address)
  - 306 distinct TCP connections opened from 10.8.15.133, running continuously from t+134.8s through the end of the capture (t+1962s)
  - 304 GET, 3 POST, 1 HEAD requests, virtually all to path `/`
  - Static, spoofed legacy user-agent on every request: `Mozilla / 5.0 (compatible; MSIE 6.0; Windows NT 5.1; SV1; .NET CLR 1.0.3705)` — anachronistic for a host running Windows 10/Edge 127, a strong bot/malware fingerprint
  - Response/request bodies are high-entropy binary data (not parseable as HTTP text), consistent with an encrypted C2/tasking protocol

## 4. Traffic ruled out as unrelated / benign

For completeness: BITS-driven downloads to `msedge.b.tlu.dl.delivery.mp.microsoft.com` (Microsoft Delivery Optimization, legitimate CDN IP 199.232.210.172) and the Adobe ARM check to `acroipm2.adobe.com` (`/assets/Owner/arm/ProcessMAU.txt`) are standard Windows/Adobe background update traffic and show no behavioral tie to the phishing/C2 chain above. They are noted only to explain why they were excluded as IOCs.

## 5. Summary of attack chain

1. User `plucero` on `DESKTOP-H8ALZBV` (10.8.15.133) browses to fake FedEx tracking page `quote.checkfedexexp.com`.
2. Page serves a ZIP containing an obfuscated, garbage-padded `.js` downloader (`Invoice-876597035-003-8331775-8334138.js`), consistent with GootLoader-style tradecraft (behavioral attribution only).
3. Script executes via WSH, sleeps ~60 seconds, then establishes persistent HTTP beaconing to hardcoded C2 `72.5.43.29:80` using a spoofed legacy-IE user-agent, continuing for the remainder of the capture.

**Recommended actions:** isolate 10.8.15.133 from the network, block `72.5.43.29`, `quote.checkfedexexp.com`, and `business.checkfedexexp.com` at the perimeter, reset credentials for `plucero`, and image the host for full disk forensics (script and payload not recoverable beyond what's in this pcap).
